question.problem:
Solve the following congruence

$$
4x-25≡20\,(\text{mod}\,21),
$$

expressing your answer as a nonnegative integer smaller than $21.$

*Hint: You may wish to use trial and error to find the appropriate multiplicative inverse.*

$x≡$
{{field-1}}$\,(\text{mod}\,21)$
question.worked_solution:
First, we reduce our congruence to a congruence of the form $ax≡b,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x-25 & ≡20\, & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 4x-25+25 & ≡20+25\, & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 4x & ≡45\, & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 4x & ≡2\cdot 21+3\, & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 4x & ≡3\, & (\text{mod}\,21)\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that a linear congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n)$ has a unique solution modulo $n$ if and only if $\text{gcd}(a,n)=1.$

In the given congruence, we have $a=4$ and $n=21$, and

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(4,21)=1.
$$

So, our congruence does indeed have a unique solution.

To find the solution, we need to multiply both sides of the equation by the multiplicative inverse of $4\,(\text{mod}\,21).$ To find the inverse of $4\,(\text{mod}\,21)$, we compute the exponents of $4\,(\text{mod}\,21)$ until we get a result of $1\,(\text{mod}\,21):$

$$
\begin{aligned}{4}^{2} & ≡16 &  & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ {4}^{3} & ≡16\cdot 4≡64≡3\cdot 21+1≡1 &  & (\text{mod}\,21)\end{aligned}
$$

So, $16\cdot 4≡1\,(\text{mod}\,21),$ which means that $16$ is the multiplicative inverse of $4$ (modulo $21$).

Now, multiplying both sides of our congruence by $16,$ we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}4x & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 16\cdot 4x & ≡16\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ (16\cdot 4)x & ≡48 &  & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ 1\cdot x & ≡6+2\cdot 21 &  & (\text{mod}\,21) \\ x & ≡6 &  & (\text{mod}\,21)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $x≡6\,(\text{mod}\,21).$
